scope: 5 reversed protosegments (segmentids 0016558, 0343093-0343096)
description: Prod doesn't reverse these protosegments: two or more reversed protosegments touch one segment, and prod's sequential updates flip its fields back and forth until they cancel out. Ours reverses them.

scope: 10 non-street segments inside Randall's Island, left and right zip
description: Prod leaves both zip codes blank; ours fills 10035, the only zip on the island, from the spatial fallback.

scope: Curve flag on compound-curve shoreline, subway and rail segments
description: Ours flags these curves irregular (I) where prod is blank: prod's irregular-curve test doesn't work on compound curves.

scope: BOE LGC pointer on segments with two-digit LGC codes
description: Prod's pointer is its default 1 where ours points at the right LGC: prod mis-parses two-digit LGC codes. 567 LION records on 26c.

scope: Segment sequence number on non-street features
description: Sequence numbers for non-street features are generated each build and don't match prod's. They only need to be unique within LION.

scope: altnames rows for Join_IDs only one side's LION carries
description: 10 altnames rows on 26c belong to Join_IDs that only one side's LION has, so they follow the LION differences rather than an altnames rule.

scope: Join_ID padding on the lion layer
description: The spec makes a non-SAF Join_ID 15 characters, ending in two spaces. Prod's lion layer drops the padding (its own altnames layer keeps it); ours keeps it. The comparison ignores the padding.

scope: Coincident segment count where a subway or rail segment nearly coincides with a centerline, about 10 records
description: Prod counts a subway or rail segment against a centerline only when Esri's shape-equality test says the two are equal; ours matches them geometrically (midpoints within 1 ft for centerlines, 0.001 ft for subway and rail). The two disagree on near-identical curved or extra-vertex geometry, so the count differs by 1. Prod also writes 0 on 4 centerlines where the spec floors the count at 1; ours keeps the floor.

scope: House-number fields on generic segments
description: The spec zeroes all eight house-number fields on generic segments, and ours does; prod has real values on 5,781 of them on 26c. The legacy rule is a manually run cleanup tool, which likely misses segments changed since it last ran.

scope: Left/right AtomicPolygon and the fields derived from it, on about 100 segments
description: Ours takes a segment's side AtomicPolygons from the AtomicPolygon edges it runs along; prod's 2 ft probe overshoots into the polygon behind where the adjacent one is shallow (corners, slivers). Census, district and locational-status fields differ on those segments. Where the probe lands in another borough's AtomicPolygon (segment 0036461, a Queens shoreline with a Manhattan proto-segment), prod also marks the segment a borough boundary, takes that side's zip, and blanks the out-of-borough side.

scope: 2 LION records reviewed one by one (236590241972, 416140101502)
description: Each record was checked by hand against source (Aug 2026) and ours is right. 2 of them differ on 26c; the others are now covered by CSCL-LION-14 or no longer differ.

scope: Special address flag on ramp protosegment, segment 174704 (Queens)
description: Prod prints B on an R-type ramp protosegment, carried over from its centerline record; the legacy rule says ramps never carry the flag. Ours is blank.

scope: SAF rows of SECURITY_LEVEL 3 CommonPlaces (5 on 26c)
description: Prod's SAF dat drops CommonPlaces with SECURITY_LEVEL 3, but its LION gdb still writes their SAF replicant rows (and counts them in SegCount). Ours copies prod: kept in the LION gdb, dropped from the SAF dat. Whether the gdb should drop them too is a question for GR.

scope: Part count, SHAPE_Length and outline on nynta2020, nycdta2020, nypp and nypuma2020, and a few nycc and nymc districts
description: Prod's polygons carry hairline slivers, about 0.0001 ft wide and under 0.3 sq ft each, along their outlines, as separate parts and as spikes off a ring: 460 parts on nynta2020, 356 on nycdta2020, 207 on nypp and 6 on nypuma2020. They add parts and SHAPE_Length but no area. Ours has none.

scope: nybid BIDs 44 and 56; nyhez zones 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and X; nycdwi districts 484 and 502
description: These source polygons are invalid (rings that cross or sit inside another ring). Prod publishes them as is; ours publishes them made valid. SHAPE_Area matches; the geometry and part counts differ.

scope: nycb2010(wi) on 12-14 blocks and nycb2020(wi) on 6-7; nyct2010wi/nyct2020wi tract 1000100; nycc/nyccwi districts 38 and 47; nymc/nymcwi 301, 305 and 404
description: Prod's census block and tract, council district and municipal court layers disagree with the current AtomicPolygons in a few places, and with prod's own ThinLION, ThinED and LION. Most weren't regenerated after recent AtomicPolygon edits. Three blocks are the same kind of disagreement: 10223003005 is keyed to tract 022300, which doesn't exist (the AtomicPolygon and prod's LION say 10223013005); water block 10001001000, and so water tract 1000100, reaches 1,417 sq ft past every AtomicPolygon; and 39901000008 includes AtomicPolygon 3990100031, whose block is 0007.

scope: Generic and physical records whose ID is deleted on another segment, 12 records on 26c
description: Prod drops any G or P record whose generic or physical ID is deleted anywhere in the edit journal (IsSegmentdeleted in LDFExtractHelper). One generic or physical ID spans many segments, so this drops reassignments LION shows took effect, e.g. segment 0003939's generic 192146 to 192147 and segment 0215581's 102207 to 192223. Ours only counts a delete on the same node pair. On 26c: 6 G/P reassignments, 2 splits and 4 merges ours publishes and prod doesn't; every other S, G and P record matches.

scope: Cumulative record number
description: Record numbers should run on across editions; prod's own sequence has a hand-entry gap (25B to 25C). Ours continues from the previous edition's header, so it drifts if prod's does.

scope: ABCEGNPX G/N/X side AtomicPolygon, 1 row per file each for placeids 1031192 and 1041121
description: Prod places a CommonPlace point within the source's XY tolerance (0.0002 ft) of an AtomicPolygon boundary in the lowest-OBJECTID AtomicPolygon within that tolerance (Esri treats the point as on the boundary). Ours applies the same rule and matches prod on every other point; on these two prod took the higher-OBJECTID AtomicPolygon.

scope: ABCEGNPX, segment 9017010
description: Prod includes an AltSegmentData row with a blank ALT_SEGDATA_TYPE, as the legacy code does; ours leaves it out, following spec Table 13.

scope: ABCEGNPX, 1 duplicate-key group per file
description: Ours writes two rows where prod writes one: placeid 551, whose street code has two principal names in source. The keyed comparison can't see it.

scope: SND, Enders and Exception rows only one side has
description: Prod was built from a newer CSCL extract than ours (inferred from code sequencing; no newer extract to check against). Once filed as stale prod entries.

scope: Police precinct, sector and patrol borough on 4 AtomicPolygons
description: When an AtomicPolygon's centroid falls outside it, prod reads police geography at Esri's label point (IArea.QueryLabelPoint), an undocumented interior point; ours takes the precinct, sector and patrol borough covering most of the AtomicPolygon. The two agree on 1,578 of the 1,582 AtomicPolygons that take this path. Two of the four are water AtomicPolygons split between two precincts, where Esri's label point lands in the smaller share; the other two differ only on sector.
